title: Tenant runway GPU budgeting and KV eviction crunch simulator
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Build a simulator and evaluation harness to compute per-tenant GPU runway (headroom) under mixed workloads and continuous batching, validate a hybrid offline-online budgeter that assigns soft watermarks for weights/KV/activations, and exercise a novel ephemeral activation compression pool and preemptible activation slots. Goal is fewer unexpected OOMs, predictable tail latency, and lower token-unit cost without increasing customer-visible failures.
acceptance_criteria: Simulator can replay 14 days of production trace slices with arrival patterns, model mix, and tenant priorities
Produce per-tenant runway curves (probability of OOM vs headroom) and recommend a soft-watermark policy param set
Validated eviction policy that uses eviction score (priority decay + recency + size) reduces customer-visible OOM rate by >=25% in simulation versus current baseline
Ephemeral activation compression pool reduces average activation footprint by >=18% for long-context requests without degrading latency SLA by >5% in simulated latency distribution
Implementation proposal and RFC for runtime changes with rollout steps and monitoring dashboards
steps: Instrument production trace export and sanitize PII (data team) - done
Design simulator architecture (sampling engine, allocator model, KV model, compression model)
Implement allocator that models weights (static), KV cache (LRU+priority decay), activations (dynamic, compressible), and headroom accounting
Run baseline replay and validate against historical incident windows
Experiment with hybrid budgeter (offline quantile forecasts + online short-horizon adjustments)
Evaluate eviction scoring variants and compression thresholds
Draft RFC with runtime API, observability signals, and canary plan
tradeoffs: Aggressive compression reduces memory but adds CPU latency and variability; acceptable when latency SLO budget exists
Soft watermarks reduce OOMs but can increase tail latency due to extra cache misses and evictions; needs careful per-model tuning
Preemptible activation slots improve overall throughput for high-priority tenants but require graceful degradation logic in SDKs/clients
Simulator fidelity vs speed: detailed GPU-level model increases accuracy but slows iteration; settle on configurable fidelity modes

metrics_to_monitor: KV churn rate (evictions/sec) and re-fetch token cost
simulation_config_summary: Replay mode: 7d sample -> 14d full. Models: mix of chat-7b/13b and embed-2.5b. GPU targets: A100-80GB and H100-80GB. Continuous batching parameters: target batch latency 30ms, max batch size 64. Compression: adaptive FP16->INT8 with CPU decompression budget capped at 10% of request CPU time. Eviction: LRU baseline, candidate: priority-decay + size_penalty. Policy tuning grid: soft_watermark in [0.06,0.12,0.18]; preemptible_slots in [0,2,4].
